title: Canonical section algebras and open Proj maps glue over an affine base cover
statement: Let $h:Z\to S$ be a quasi-compact separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $S=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ be an affine open covering, put $Z_i=h^{-1}(U_i)$, $h_i:Z_i\to U_i$, and $N_i=N|_{Z_i}$. Tensor powers use [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], direct image means $h_*F(V)=\Gamma(h^{-1}(V),F)$, and $h^*$ is module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. For each $i$, suppose the canonical section algebra $\mathcal A_i=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}(h_i)_*N_i^{\otimes d}$ is a quasi-coherent graded algebra [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra, def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], and let $\psi_i:h_i^*\mathcal A_i\to\bigoplus_{d\geq0}N_i^{\otimes d}$ be its adjunction evaluation. For such an evaluation, $U(\psi_i)$ denotes the union of the loci where a positive-degree component is surjective, and $r_i:U(\psi_i)\to\operatorname{Proj}_{U_i}(\mathcal A_i)$ denotes its canonical map [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map, def-nagata-relative-proj]. Assume $U(\psi_i)=Z_i$ and every $r_i$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Then $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}h_*N^{\otimes d}$ is a quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal O_S$-algebra. For its adjunction evaluation $\psi$, there are canonical graded isomorphisms $\mathcal A|_{U_i}\simeq\mathcal A_i$ identifying the restricted evaluation with $\psi_i$ and, under $\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal A)\times_SU_i\simeq\operatorname{Proj}_{U_i}(\mathcal A_i)$, identifying the restricted generation loci and canonical maps with $U(\psi_i)$ and $r_i$. Consequently $U(\psi)=Z$, and $r_{N,\psi}:Z\to\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal A)$ is an open immersion. All section algebras, evaluations and canonical maps in these comparisons are the ordinary Zariski scheme constructions.

proof.text: Apply exists_section_algebra_open_cover_descent to construct A and choose the normalized coefficientwise open comparisons D_i. Their section formulas are definitionally canonicalSectionOpenPull, so each pair is the existing OpenComparison structure.

Apply section_canonical_map_open_descent to A, D_i and their section formulas, using the given full local generation and canonical maps. This supplies full global generation, a canonical map r and each restriction equation.

For each i, D_i.isPullback identifies its Proj comparison as a base change of U_i → S, so the comparison is an open immersion. The restriction equation and the assumed openness of r_local i show that inclusion_i followed by r is an open immersion.

If r(x)=r(y), the structural equation r followed by A.relProjHom = h gives h(x)=h(y). Choose U_i containing h(x); both x and y lie in h inverse U_i. The composite inclusion_i followed by r is an open immersion, so injectivity on that open gives x=y. Every x belongs to such an inverse-image open on which r is an open immersion. Apply IsOpenImmersion.of_forall_source_exists. Package the already constructed section comparisons and their equations.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01VJ (3) implies (5), with section-algebra/evaluation steps isolated in two strictly smaller statements and the final open-immersion gluing proved in Lean using the base-change and injective-local-source APIs.
